name: Pleat House
description: A folding retail fitting-room rental pitch.

slides.title: PLEAT HOUSE
items: A fitting room that travels flat.
Illustrative seed pitch

slides.title: A room inside a room
items: The first installation goes into a borrowed gallery. The booth stands clear of the clothes rail, and the host checks sightlines from the queue before opening.
The same screen closes at the end of the event and returns to inventory for the next booking.

slides.title: The lease lasts four days.
items: The fitting room takes a week.
A pop-up producer books a temporary shop, then hires a carpenter, buys sheet goods and arranges removal. A simple privacy enclosure becomes another trade to schedule.
Our first buyer opens at least six short retail events each year.

slides.title: One case. Two feet.
items: The kit arrives as a folded screen, two feet and a closure strap. On return, staff inspect the paper edges and replace a damaged segment before the next dispatch.
Pack-out checklist

slides.title: One weekend on the books
items: Rental revenue per three-day event, excluding delivery billed at cost.
$180 variable cost
Cleaning, repair reserve and handling leave $360 contribution per booking. At a $1,440 build cost, four bookings recover the unit investment before overhead.

slides.title: The fourth booking pays for the booth
items: Cumulative contribution after build cost • illustrative dollars
By booking six, the booth has contributed $720 beyond its build cost. Storage and fixed staff costs still come out of that balance.

slides.title: Open the fold.
items: A continuous folded wall curves back on itself to screen the entrance. Two removable feet hold its ends. The host chooses the orientation for the shop floor.
The prototype is for indoor retail. Stability, clear entry and local accessibility requirements are checked at the venue before use.

slides.title: Why rent the fold?
items: Curtain rail
Lowest upfront cost. The producer still sources fabric, weights and a frame and owns the teardown.
Built partition
A fit for long residencies with a dedicated build crew. A one-week lease leaves little time to recover fabrication and removal costs.
Pleat House
One reusable object with a known pack size. The buyer pays for event dates and hands back the kit on collection.

slides.title: Follow the producer
items: 30 agencies
At eight suitable events per agency and two booths per event, the starting territory represents 480 annual bookings. At $540 each, that is $259,200 in modeled rental revenue.
The route to the rack
Invite producers to a one-day setup trial. Quote the next three dates together and reserve stock only when a deposit lands.

slides.title: What breaks first?
items: Edge wear
Record dents after each return. A replaceable outer segment must be cheaper than retiring the whole wall.
Changeover time
Time a two-person setup and pack-down at every pilot. The pass condition is under twenty minutes each way.
Availability
Book a second weekend only when inspection and repair can finish before the next dispatch.

slides.title: From sample to rental fleet
items: Mira Song / industrial design
Mira owns fold geometry, foot stability and the repair manual. She will release the second tooling run after ten units pass repeated handling tests.
Rafi Lowe / event operations
Rafi owns dispatch, cleaning and agency contracts. He will pilot three venues in one city before adding a second delivery route.

slides.title: Open for the weekend.
items: $650k pre-seed
$300k for tooling and fleet, $200k for operations and $150k for agency trials. In twelve months the target is 60 paid bookings and six repeat agencies.
Illustrative venture and financial model.
